title: What If You Never Needed to Sleep Again? The Rules, the Science and the Price
description:
3 a.m. The city is asleep, and you haven't slept in forty days — and you feel amazing. In a week you'll have 56 more hours than everyone else. In a month you'll discover the night is a separate city. And in a year you'll understand what sleep is really for.

A second-person story: four rules, what science says happens to a normal person without sleep, and the price nobody thinks about.

00:00 Forty Nights
01:04 The Wish List
02:06 The Rules
03:10 The Night City
04:12 The First Year
05:11 What Science Says
06:30 No More Dreams
07:14 The Price
08:10 Other People's Nights
09:13 Morning

Sources: Randy Gardner, 1964 (264 hours awake); Williamson & Feyer, 2000 (17–19 h awake ≈ 0.05% BAC); Dawson & Reid, 1997, Nature (24 h awake ≈ 0.10% BAC); Rechtschaffen et al. (sleep deprivation in rats); Xie et al., 2013, Science (brain waste clearance during sleep).
This is a thought experiment, not medical advice. Don't try to stay awake — it's dangerous.
Voice: ElevenLabs. Script and animation made with the help of AI.

Rules of the Impossible — a new "What if…" every week.
